5-192 BRIEF. APPLICATION OF Arunas J. Legard FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Edwin Joseph Legard IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Tacoma, Wash. POST-OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: Tacoma, Wm. Date of enrollment, Feb. 13, 1920 Term of enrollment, Three (3) years. NAME OF PERSON ARRANGING FOR THE TRANSFER: Arunas J. Legard Position, APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Jacoma, Tex., of Edwin Joseph Legard, m-10, I, Amos J. Legard of Jacoma, Wash., State of Wash., do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to his enrollment in said school for a period of 3 years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Jacoma, Tex., on March 6, 1909 (Date), that the father, Amos J. Legard, is a white person of the Creole tribe located at Chehalis Agency; that he left the tribe about 1907 (Approximate date); that the mother, Louise Legard, is a white person of the Chehalis tribe located at Chehalis Agency, and left the tribe about 1907 (Approximate date) that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:
NAME OF SCHOOL—PUBLIC GOVERNMENT, OR MISSION. LOCATED AT DATE OF ENROLLMENT DATE OF DECHARGE GRADE
Furwood 2nd
Should the child be returned home for one of the vacation periods of this enrollment at my request I further agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. I further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Chehalis school on or before the last day of the vacation period of absence. I further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient funds to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the child fail to return to school at such time as may have been agreed upon by myself and the superintendent of the school, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the child so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government. This 13th day of Feb., 1920 Two witnesses: Amos J. Legard P.O. (Affix signature of parent, guardian, or next of kin) AFFIDAVIT. I, Amos J. Legard, do hereby swear that the statements made in the above application are true. Sworn to and subscribed before me this 13th day of Feb., 1920 C.E. The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." (Act of August 1, 1914.) EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; these children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission from the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse to or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year." (27 Stat. L., 635. See 2 Dec. Comp., 308.)
